BURHAN:v3p284/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p284/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p284/r5.claim: The affirmation formula reverses the order of Hārūn and Mūsā in Ṭā Hā and al-Shuʿarāʾ; the author notes the contrast without giving a reason here.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p49/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p49/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p49/r4.claim: The magicians recognized the staff's miracle and fell in prostration; they already suspected Moses's sign was not magic and had been pressured to face him.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p49/r4.anchor: what Moses (sws) would present is not magic

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p49/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p49/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p49/r5.claim: Prostration then signaled recognition of someone's mastery of a skill; the magicians went further and publicly professed faith in the God of Moses and Aaron.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p49/r5.anchor: Falling down in prostration in this way in those times

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p49/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p49/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p49/r6.claim: Their public profession of faith led Pharaoh to make a new verbal attack to influence the crowd.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p49/r6.anchor: announced in the whole gathering that they have professed faith

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356#2/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356#2/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356#2/r12.claim: The text says the magicians were cast into prostration rather than simply saying they prostrated, conveying the sudden irresistible effect of the miracle.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356#2/r12.anchor: وجاء التركيب فألقي السحرة ولم يأت فسجدوا كأنه جاءهم أمر وأزعجهم وأخذهم فصنع بهم ذلك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356#2/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356#2/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356#2/r13.claim: The ordering of Moses and Aaron differs between al-Aʿraf and this passage.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356#2/r13.anchor: وقدم موسى في الأعراف وأخر هارون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358/r1.claim: The order of the names serves the verse endings; Moses is also the one associated with the staff miracle. The order of coordinated names does not itself require sequence.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358/r1.anchor: لأجل الفواصل ولكون موسى هو المنسوب إليه العصا التي ظهر فيها ما ظهر من الإعجاز، وأخر موسى لأجل الفواصل أيضا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358/r2.claim: One possibility is that two groups voiced the names in opposite orders; since they share the same meaning, both wordings can be attributed to all the magicians.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358/r2.anchor: على أنه يحتمل أن يكون القولان من قائلين نطقت طائفة بقولهم رب موسى وهارون، وطائفة بقولهم: رب هارون وموسى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358/r3.claim: One view says Aaron is named first here because he was older than Moses.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358/r3.anchor: وقيل: قدم هارون هنا لأنه كان أكبر سنا من موسى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358/r4.claim: Another view says they put Aaron first to counter Pharaoh’s boast that he had raised Moses, whom he had brought up.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358/r4.anchor: وقيل لأن فرعون كان ربى موسى فبدؤوا بهارون ليزول تمويه فرعون أنه ربى موسى فيقول أنا ربيته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358/r5.claim: Naming the Lord of Moses and Aaron explicitly asserts their belief in the God of these two, while Pharaoh had previously claimed to be lord of the worlds.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358/r5.anchor: وقالوا: رب هارون وموسى ولم يكتفوا بقولهم برب العالمين للنص على أنهم آمنوا برب هذين وكان فيما قبل يزعم أنه رب العالمين

TABATABAI:20:49-79#10/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79#10/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49-79#10/r4.claim: The passive wording that the magicians were made to fall prostrate, instead of saying they prostrated, depicts divine power subduing and overwhelming them until they had no choice.
TABATABAI:20:49-79#10/r4.anchor: بالبناء للمفعول دون أن يقال فسجد السحرة إشاره إلى إذلال القدرة الإلهية لهم وغشيان الحق بظهوره إياهم

TABATABAI:20:49-79#10/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79#10/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49-79#10/r5.claim: Their confession names the Lord through both Moses and Aaron, thereby testifying both to God's lordship and to the two prophets' messengership.
TABATABAI:20:49-79#10/r5.anchor: ليكون فيه الشهادة على ربوبيته تعالى ورسالة موسى وهارون معا

TABATABAI:20:49-79#10/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79#10/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49-79#10/r6.claim: The phrase they said is uncoordinated because it answers an implied question about what the magicians said.
TABATABAI:20:49-79#10/r6.anchor: من غير عطف لكونه كالجواب لسؤال مقدر كأنه قيل فما قالوا

RAZI-FULL:v22p75/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p75/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p75/r1.claim: To block Pharaoh's claim that “Lord of the worlds” meant himself, the magicians named Aaron before Moses: Pharaoh claimed to have raised Moses and thus to be his lord.
RAZI-FULL:v22p75/r1.anchor: لأن فرعون كان يدعي ربوبيته لموسى بناء على أنه رباه

RAZI-FULL:v22p76/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p76/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p76/r1.claim: The magicians had seen God favor Aaron and Moses with great miracles and high ranks, so they confessed to the Lord of both.
RAZI-FULL:v22p76/r1.anchor: لما شاهدوا أن الله تعالى خصهما بتلك المعجزات العظيمة والدرجات الشريفة لا جرم قالوا

RAZI-FULL:v22p76/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p76/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p76/r2.claim: Seeing their prostration and confession, Pharaoh feared that others would imitate them and believe in God and His messenger.
RAZI-FULL:v22p76/r2.anchor: ثم إن فرعون لما شاهد منهم السجود والإقرار خاف أن يصير ذلك سببا لاقتداء سائر الناس بهم

STUDYQURAN:20:70/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:70/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:70/r1.claim: For the sorcerers’ prostration and declaration of faith, the commentary directs readers to 7:119–22.

TABRISI:20:71-74/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:71-74/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:71-74/r1.claim: The clause omits the preceding events: Moses cast his staff and it swallowed what the magicians had made; then the magicians fell prostrate.
TABRISI:20:71-74/r1.anchor: ههنا محذوف وهو فألقى عصاه وتلقف ما صنعوا فألقي السحرة سجدا

TABRISI:20:71-74/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:71-74/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:71-74/r2.claim: The passive expression means that the magicians prostrated themselves.
TABRISI:20:71-74/r2.anchor: أي سجدوا { وقالوا آمنا برب هارون وموسى

TABRISI:20:71-74/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:71-74/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:71-74/r3.claim: They attributed God to Aaron and Moses because the two called people to Him and were His messengers.
TABRISI:20:71-74/r3.anchor: أضافوه سبحانه إليهما لدعائهما إليه وكونهما رسولين له.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p462/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p462/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p462/r1.claim: The magicians prostrated after Moses did what he was commanded; details of the staff swallowing their work were omitted because they appear in 7 and 26.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p462/r1.anchor: - وقوله تعالى: {فألقي السحرة سجدا} ففعل ما أمر به موسى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p462/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p462/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p462/r2.claim: The account of what happened in this verse was already covered in the commentary on al-Aʿrāf.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p462/r2.anchor: وما يقع من الكلام في تفسير هذه الآية قد سبق في سورة الأعراف

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:70/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:70/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:70/r1.claim: The magicians fell down prostrate to God and declared belief in the Lord of Aaron and Moses.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:70/r1.anchor: خروا ساجدين لله تعالى { قالوا آمنا برب هارون وموسى }

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266#2/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266#2/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266#2/r1.claim: The magicians fell in prostration and declared belief in Aaron and Moses' Lord.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266#2/r1.anchor: فألقي السحرة سجدا قالوا آمنا برب هارون وموسى {70} قال} [طه: 70-71] فرعون.

QASHANI:20:64-70/r8.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:64-70/r8.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:64-70/r8.claim: The magicians prostrate as fair-minded people who acknowledge the truth after recognizing the proof, miracle, and decisive argument.
QASHANI:20:64-70/r8.anchor: { فألقي السحرة سجدا } منصفين مذعنين مقرين بكونه على الحق لما عرفوا من صدق البينة

QASHANI:20:64-70/r9.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:64-70/r9.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:64-70/r9.claim: They profess certain faith after unveiling God's universal lordship; they name Aaron and Moses because divine attributes are manifested in them according to capacity, through them rather than independently.
QASHANI:20:64-70/r9.anchor: { قالوا آمنا } الإيمان اليقيني لأنهم كوشفوا بالحق فعرفوا ربوبيته للكل

QASHANI:20:64-70/r10.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:64-70/r10.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:64-70/r10.claim: Extraordinary acts arise from material combinations, prepared images attracting celestial forces, or soul-power: a prophetic envoy's miracle or a non-prophetic saint's gift.
QASHANI:20:64-70/r10.anchor: واعلم أن الساحر أقرب الناس استعدادا من النبي لأن مبادىء خوارق العادات أمور ثلاثة

QASHANI:20:64-70/r11.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:64-70/r11.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:64-70/r11.claim: A miracle differs from a saint's gift because it is accompanied by challenge and opposition, while the gift is not.
QASHANI:20:64-70/r11.anchor: والفرق بينهما أن الإعجاز مقارن للتحدي والمعارضة دون الكرامة

QASHANI:20:64-70/r12.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:64-70/r12.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:64-70/r12.claim: The sorcerer begins with strong influence but weakens by turning toward nature and away from the higher source; a prophet or saint strengthens through divine orientation, so the sorcerer is overcome and often recognizes and accepts the prophet unless natural inclination erases his capacity.
QASHANI:20:64-70/r12.anchor: ومن المقبل على الدنيا المعرض عن العالم الأعلى سحر، فكانت نفس الساحر في بدء فطرتها قوية مخصوصة بهيئات مؤثرة في هذا العالم

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r1.claim: Israelite presence in Egypt and Moses' effort to lead them back to their homeland created political anxiety for Pharaoh's government and a psychological warfare setting.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r1.anchor: İsrâiloğulları’nın Mısır’daki varlığının ve Hz. Mûsâ tarafından eski yurtlarına götürülmeleri için ortaya konan çabanın Firavun yönetimi nezdinde oluşturduğu siyasî kaygılar

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r5.claim: The magicians themselves recognized the evident truth and believed, while Pharaoh and his men persisted in unbelief.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r5.anchor: bizzat bu silâhı kullanan sihirbazlar dahi apaçık hakikati gördükleri için imana geldikleri halde Firavun ve adamları inkârcılıktaki inatlarını sürdürdüler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r7.claim: After tasting faith, the magicians recognized that no worldly reward, even being spared, could compare with the happiness of the afterlife and dared to say so openly.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r7.anchor: idrak edip bunu açıkça ifade etme cesaretini gösterdiler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r8.claim: The commentary points readers to compare the Qur'anic account with the Biblical account of the episode.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r8.anchor: bu olayla ilgili bilgilerin Kitâb-ı Mukaddes’tekilerle karşılaştırılması için bk. A‘râf 7/103-126

QUSHAYRI:v2p266/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p266/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p266/r5.claim: Seeing the sign, the magicians prostrated in faith, while Pharaoh and his people were left defeated.
QUSHAYRI:v2p266/r5.anchor: فسجدوا لله مؤمنين ، وانقلب فرعون وقومه خائبين

QUSHAYRI:v2p266/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p266/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p266/r7.claim: The magicians moved from swearing by Pharaoh's might to swearing by God, becoming believers and righteous within a single day.
QUSHAYRI:v2p266/r7.anchor: وبعدما كانوا يقسمون بعزة فرعون صاروا يحلفون بالله

QUSHAYRI:v2p266/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p266/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p266/r9.claim: The inward suns of gnosis and lights of divine care let them see God inwardly, confess faith, and prostrate in their hearts before what they witnessed.
QUSHAYRI:v2p266/r9.anchor: لما طلعت في أسرارهم شموس العرفان ، وانبسطت عليهم أنوار العناية أبصروا الحق سبحانه بأسرارهم

BURHAN:v1p55/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p55/r1.speaker: مخالفوهم
BURHAN:v1p55/r1.claim: Many opponents claim the Qur’an uses sajʿ as a rhetorical excellence; they cite the changed order of Aaron and Moses as evidence of adjusting words to cadences.
BURHAN:v1p55/r1.anchor: وذهب كثير من مخالفيهم إلى إثبات السجع فى القرآن وزعموا أن ذلك مما تبين فيه فضل الكلام

BURHAN:v1p55/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p55/r2.speaker: مخالفوهم
BURHAN:v1p55/r2.claim: They argue that unlike poetry, whose meter must be intentional, sajʿ is too frequent in the Qur’an to be accidental; they define it as successive speech on one meter.
BURHAN:v1p55/r2.anchor: قالوا وهذا يفارق أمر الشعر لأنه لا يجوز أن يقع فى الخطاب إلا مقصودا إليه وإذا وقع غير مقصود إليه كان دون القدر الذى نسميه شعرا

BURHAN:v1p55/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p55/r5.speaker: القاضي
BURHAN:v1p55/r5.claim: The reversed order of Moses and Aaron is not for rhyme: retelling one story with different wording and order while preserving meaning is difficult eloquence that exposes the imitators’ inability.
BURHAN:v1p55/r5.anchor: ولهذا أعيدت كثير من القصص فى مواضع كثيرة مختلفة على ترتيبات متفاوتة

BURHAN:v3p233/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p233/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p233/r1.claim: The default order places subject before object, topic before predicate, and possessor before its circumstantial phrase unless a reason favors change.
BURHAN:v3p233/r1.anchor: أحدها أن يكون أصله التقديم ولا مقتضى للعدول عنه

BURHAN:v3p233/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p233/r8.speaker: السكاكي
BURHAN:v3p233/r8.claim: Al-Sakkaki treats Aaron's mention before Moses as an order chosen for cadence, although Moses has the stronger claim to precedence.
BURHAN:v3p233/r8.anchor: وجعل منه السكاكي 1 ﴿ آمنا برب هارون وموسى

BURHAN:v3p255/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p255/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p255/r3.claim: The Taha order puts Aaron before Moses to suit the verse endings, despite Moses' precedence in merit elsewhere.
BURHAN:v3p255/r3.anchor: فقد جاء هارون وموسى في سورة طه بتقديم هارون قلنا لتناسب رءوس الآي

ZAJJAJ:v3p367#2/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p367#2/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p367#2/r3.claim: Sujjadan is accusative as a circumstantial expression and describes an expected state: they fell intending to prostrate, before they were yet prostrating.
ZAJJAJ:v3p367#2/r3.anchor: (سجدا) منصوب على الحال، وهي أيضا حال مقدرة

ASAD-NOTES:20:70#n50/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:70#n50/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:70#n50/r1.claim: Asad points to 7:117–119 for the parallel account of the sorcerers' defeat.

ASAD-NOTES:20:70#n51/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:70#n51/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:70#n51/r1.claim: Asad directs readers to note 90 on 7:120 for the parallel account of the sorcerers' response.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8/r2.claim: The order of Musa and Harun changes across the two scenes so each verse ends in the cadence suited to its sura; Ta-Ha ends with Musa and its alif.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8/r2.anchor: بتقديم موسى على هارون، فيجعل لكمة (هارون) نهاية الفاصلة انسجاماً مع الفواصل السابقة واللاحقة، ومرة يقول

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8/r7.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8/r7.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8/r7.claim: Cadence does not act alone: the wording and order also answer the meaning in each context, so one passage is not forced at the expense of another.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8/r7.anchor: فلم يَجُرْ موطن على آخر وهذا غاية الإعجاز ونهاية الحسن في الكلام

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8#2/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8#2/r1.claim: Although the verse endings fit the names' order, the narratives also call for Aaron before Moses in Ta-Ha and Moses before Aaron in al-Shuara.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8#2/r1.anchor: قدم في (طه) ذكر هرون وفي (الشعراء) ذكر موسى

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8#2/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8#2/r5.claim: The initials add a further fit: Ta-Ha ends with hāʾ, the first letter of Hārūn, while Ṭā-Sīn-Mīm ends with mīm, the first of Mūsā; each lacks the other's initial.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8#2/r5.anchor: الحرف الأخير من (طه) هو الهاء، وهو أول حروف هرون وليس فيها حرف من حروف موسى

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p91/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p91/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p91/r3.claim: The source asks why the order of Aaron and Moses changes between Ta-Ha and Shuara and whether the change serves the fāṣila; this segment gives no answer.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p91/r3.anchor: لماذا التقديم والتأخير وهل هو للفاصلة القرآنية؟

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p541/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p541/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p541/r4.claim: He raises, without answering here, whether the reversed order of Aaron and Moses in Taha and al-Shu'ara is due to the verse endings.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p541/r4.anchor: لماذا التقديم والتأخير وهل هو للفاصلة القرآنية؟

ALUSI-FULL:v16p230#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p230#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p230#2/r1.claim: The ف implies omitted events: fear ended, Moses cast the staff, it became a serpent and swallowed their ropes and staffs, then the magicians recognized the miracle.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p230#2/r1.anchor: عن التصريح أى فزال الخوف وألقى ما فى يمينه وصارت حية

ALUSI-FULL:v16p230#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p230#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p230#2/r2.claim: They fell prostrate to God in repentance, believing in God and in Moses’ mission.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p230#2/r2.anchor: فألقى السحرة على وجوههم سجدا لله تعالى تائبين مؤمنين به عز وجل وبرسالة موسى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p230#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p230#2/r3.speaker: رئيسهم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p230#2/r3.claim: Their leader says they used to defeat people while their tools remained; asking where their objects went if this were magic, they inferred a powerful, knowing Creator and Moses’ true mission.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p230#2/r3.anchor: روى أن رئيسهم قال : كنا نغلب الناس وكانت الآلات تبقى علينا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p230#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p230#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p230#2/r4.claim: They reasoned from bodily transformation to an omnipotent, knowing Creator and from the miracle through Moses to the truth of his prophethood; total annihilation is possible.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p230#2/r4.anchor: فاستدل بتغير أحوال الأجسام على الصانع القدير العليم

ALUSI-FULL:v16p230#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p230#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p230#2/r5.claim: Saying they were made to fall, rather than simply that they prostrated, shows the sight overwhelmed them; the wording evokes God’s guidance from obstinate unbelief to faith.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p230#2/r5.anchor: وفي التعبير بألقى دون فسجد إشارة إلى أنهم شاهدوا ما أزعجهم فلم يتمالكوا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p230#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p230#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p230#2/r6.claim: The phrasing also gives stylistic correspondence and conveys that they hurried to prostrate.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p230#2/r6.anchor: وفيه إيقاظ السامع لألطاف الله تعالى فى نقله من شاء من عباده

ALUSI-FULL:v16p230#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p230#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p230#2/r7.claim: It is said they did not lift their heads until they saw the Garden and Fire, reward and punishment.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p230#2/r7.anchor: من السجود حتى رأوا الجنة والنار والثواب والعقاب

ALUSI-FULL:v16p230#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p230#2/r8.speaker: عكرمة
ALUSI-FULL:v16p230#2/r8.claim: Ikrimah reports that God showed them their Garden stations while they prostrated; al-Qadi objects this compels belief and undermines moral responsibility.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p230#2/r8.anchor: عن عكرمة أنهم لما خروا سجدا أراهم الله تعالى فى سجودهم منازلهم فى الجنة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p230#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p230#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p230#2/r9.claim: Alusi replies that faith preceded the unveiling, so it did not compel them; al-Irshad says their stations were theirs in light of their plea for forgiveness.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p230#2/r9.anchor: أجيب بأنه حين كان الإيمان مقدما على هذا الكشف فلا منافاة ولا إلجاء

ALUSI-FULL:v16p230#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p230#2/r10.speaker: إرشاد العقل السليم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p230#2/r10.claim: Al-Irshad says seeing their stations does not conflict with their plea for forgiveness, since the stations were theirs conditional on that declaration.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p230#2/r10.anchor: ارشاد العقل السليم أنه لا ينافيه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p230#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p230#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p230#2/r11.claim: قالوا is a resumption, as in earlier passages.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p230#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p230#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p230#2/r12.claim: Moses comes second because he is more honored and the mission belongs primarily to him; the miracle appeared through him and the order maintains the verse’s rhyme.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p230#2/r12.anchor: تأخير موسى عليه السلام عند حكاية كلامهم المذكورة فى سورة الأعراف المقدم فيه موسى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p230#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p230#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p230#2/r13.claim: Another possibility is that this was their actual order because Aaron was older; al-Sayyid’s claim that Moses was older is a mistake.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p230#2/r13.anchor: وقدموا هرون عليه السلام بأنه أكبر سنا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p230#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p230#2/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p230#2/r14.claim: The order may avert the false inference that رب موسى means Pharaoh, who raised Moses; the al-Aʿraf ordering is the narrator’s arrangement for this reason.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p230#2/r14.anchor: وأما للمبالغة فى الاحتراز عن التوهم الباطل من جهة فرعون وقومه حيث كان فرعون ربى موسى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p230#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p230#3/r1.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v16p230#3/r1.claim: Abu Hayyan allows this and al-Aʿraf to quote two groups, each ordering the names for a different point; since their meanings match, both statements can be attributed to all. Alusi prefers this for this sūra.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p230#3/r1.anchor: وجوز أبو حيان أن يكون ما هنا قول طائفة منهم وما هناك قول أخرى وراعى كل نكتة فيما فعل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r9.claim: The magicians fell prostrate and declared faith in the Lord of Aaron and Moses.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r9.anchor: فألقي السحرة سجدا قالوا آمنا برب هارون وموسى قال آمنتم له قبل أن آذن لكم

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:70/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:70/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:70/r1.claim: The staff swallowed the tricks, making the magicians realize it was God's sign rather than magic; they fell prostrate to God in repentance and reverence.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:70/r1.anchor: فألقى فتلقفت فتحقق عند السحرة أنه ليس بسحر

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:70/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:70/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:70/r2.claim: Aaron may be named first because he was older, to fit the verse's cadence, or because Pharaoh had raised Moses and might otherwise be mistaken for the intended lord.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:70/r2.anchor: قدم هارون لكبر سنه أو لروي الآية

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:70/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:70/r3.speaker: روي
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:70/r3.claim: A report says the magicians saw Paradise and their own dwellings there while prostrating.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:70/r3.anchor: روي أنهم رأوا في سجودهم الجنة ومنازلهم فيها

BIQAI-FULL:v5p29/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29/r9.claim: The magicians rushed into submission at what they witnessed of God’s power, falling prostrate with extraordinary speed and ease.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29/r9.anchor: فبادر السحرة منهم إلى الخضوع لأمر الله ساجدين

BIQAI-FULL:v5p29/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29/r10.claim: The account omits Moses’ act of throwing the staff and the ensuing swallowing because this sūra emphasizes God’s power to soften hardened hearts.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29/r10.anchor: وحذف ذكر الإلقاء وما سببه من التلقف لأن مقصود السورة القدرة على تليين القلوب القاسية

BIQAI-FULL:v5p29#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29#2/r1.speaker: الأصبهاني
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29#2/r1.claim: Al-Aṣfahānī marvels that the magicians first cast ropes and staffs in disbelief, then soon cast themselves into prostration in gratitude, a striking contrast between the two acts.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p29#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29#2/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29#2/r2.claim: Their declaration of faith means that they truly believed and affirmed the truth.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29#2/r2.anchor: فما قالوا ؟ فقيل : { قالوا آمنا } أي صدقنا

BIQAI-FULL:v5p29#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29#2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29#2/r3.claim: Harun is named before Musa to suit this sūra’s context and foreshadow that the Qur’an will guide people who become humble supporters of the Prophet despite their former pride.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29#2/r3.anchor: ولما كان سياق هذه السورة مقتضيا لتقديم هارون عليه السلام

BIQAI-FULL:v5p29#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29#2/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29#2/r4.claim: Naming the Lord points to His favor in raising the brothers above the magicians and above Pharaoh, who claimed lordship but could not help his followers.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29#2/r4.anchor: وذكروا اسم الرب إشارة إلى أنه سبحانه أحسن إليهما بإعلاء شأنهما

BIQAI-FULL:v5p29#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29#2/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29#2/r5.claim: The magicians began the day as sorcerers and ended it as righteous witnesses, transformed by what they saw.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p29#2/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29#2/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29#2/r6.claim: The order of names reflects a meaningful progression through the minister and translator to the one who sent him; it is not an order chosen merely for rhyme.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29#2/r6.anchor: ترقيا في درج المعرفة ممن أوصل ذلك إليهم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p29#2/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29#2/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29#2/r7.claim: The Prophet criticized the disputed kind of contrived sajʿ by comparing it to the rhymed speech of pre-Islamic people or soothsayers.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29#2/r7.anchor: وقد عاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ذلك حين قال : ( سجع

BIQAI-FULL:v5p29#2/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29#2/r8.speaker: الرازي
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29#2/r8.claim: Al-Rāzī, as quoted by Abū Ḥayyān, says no Qur’anic wording is advanced or delayed for rhyme, since its inimitability lies in meaning as well as wording.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29#2/r8.anchor: قد قال الإمام فخر الدين الرازي كما حكاه عنه الشيخ

BIQAI-FULL:v5p29#2/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29#2/r9.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر الباقلاني
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29#2/r9.claim: Al-Bāqillānī reports that his school rejects sajʿ in the Qur’an: in sajʿ meaning follows the rhyme, whereas Qur’anic wording follows the intended meaning.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29#2/r9.anchor: وقال القاضي أبو بكر الباقلاني في كتاب إعجاز القرآن : ذهب

BIQAI-FULL:v5p29#2/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29#2/r10.speaker: أبو الحسن الأشعري
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29#2/r10.claim: Al-Ashʿarī also argued in several of his works against classifying Qur’anic passages as sajʿ; apparent rhyme is only an accidental likeness.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29#2/r10.anchor: وذكره أبو الحسن الأشعري في غير موضع من كتبه , ثم رد

BIQAI-FULL:v5p29#2/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29#2/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29#2/r11.claim: A passage may resemble sajʿ without being it: when meaning is complete independently, rhyme only decorates; Qur’anic wording conveys the intended meaning.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29#2/r11.anchor: لأن السجع يتبع المعنى فيه الافظ الذي يؤدي السجع

BIQAI-FULL:v5p29#2/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29#2/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29#2/r12.claim: The author points readers to his discussion at the end of al-Tawba for further argument against explaining Qur’anic word order by rhyme.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29#2/r12.anchor: وقد تقدم في آخر سورة التوبة ما ينفع جدا في هذا المرام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p260/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p260/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p260/r9.claim: The opening fa coordinates with an omitted clause: Moses threw, the staff swallowed their work, as in the command to strike the sea and its parting.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p260/r9.anchor: الفاء عاطفة على محذوف يدل عليه قوله { وألق ما في يمينك } ( طه : 69 )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p261/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p261/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p261/r1.claim: The passive means they cast themselves down, since nobody else cast them; their prostration publicly acknowledged Moses as God’s messenger.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p261/r1.anchor: وأسند الفعل إلى المجهول لأنهم لا ملقي لهم إلا أنفسهم ، فكأنه قيل : فألقوا أنفسهم سجدا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p261/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p261/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p261/r2.claim: One possible sense is that the magicians prostrated in worship of God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p261/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون سجودهم تعظيما لله تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p261/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p261/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p261/r3.claim: Another possibility is that they prostrated to honor Moses after recognizing his victory over them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p261/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون دلالة على تغلب موسى عليهم فسجدوا تعظيما له

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p261/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p261/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p261/r4.claim: They may instead have honored Pharaoh as a precaution against his violence before declaring faith.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p261/r4.anchor: ويجوز أن يريدوا به تعظيم فرعون ، جعلوه مقدمة لقولهم { ءامنا برب هارون وموسى } حذرا من بطشه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p261/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p261/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p261/r5.claim: Sujjad is the plural of sājid.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p261/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p261/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p261/r6.claim: Qālū may be a circumstantial clause, an appositional specification of what their prostration contained, or an independent opening of dialogue.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p261/r6.anchor: وجملة { قالوا } يصح أن تكون في موضع الحال ، أي ألقوا قائلين .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p261/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p261/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p261/r7.claim: They believed at that moment because, as masters of sorcery, they knew Moses’ feat was not magic but a sign from God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p261/r7.anchor: وإنما آمنوا بالله حينئذ لأنهم أيقنوا أن ما جرى على يد موسى ليس من جنس السحر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p261/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p261/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p261/r8.claim: They identified God by relation to Moses and Aaron because those were the names by which they knew him, among people who worshipped other gods, including Pharaoh.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p261/r8.anchor: وتعبيرهم عن الرب بطريق الإضافة إلى هارون وموسى لأن الله لم يكن يعرف بينهم يومئذ إلا بهذه النسبة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p261/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p261/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p261/r9.claim: Putting Aaron before Moses here and Moses before Aaron in al-Aʿrāf implies no rank: the coordinating waw conveys only their joint inclusion.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p261/r9.anchor: لا دلالة فيه على تفضيل ولا غيره ، لأن الواو العاطفة لا تفيد أكثر من مطلق الجمع في الحكم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p261/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p261/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p261/r10.claim: Al-Aʿrāf also reports their confession as belief in the Lord of all worlds; this account omits that wording because reports need not reproduce everything, only what serves the context.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p261/r10.anchor: ألا ترى أنه حكي في سورة الأعراف ( 121 ) قول السحرة { قالوا آمنا برب العالمين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p261/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p261/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p261/r11.claim: Aaron’s precedence here may be the narrator’s choice for the rhyme, rather than the order in the magicians’ original speech; another report places Moses first.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p261/r11.anchor: ووجه تقديم هارون هنا الرعاية على الفاصلة ، فالتقديم وقع في الحكاية لا في المحكي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p261/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p261/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p261/r12.claim: Alternatively, the magicians may have uttered both formulas, naming Aaron first for seniority and Moses first for his greater prophetic rank and divine speech.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p261/r12.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون تقديم هارون في هذه الآية من حكاية قول السحرة ، فيكون صدر منهم قولان

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52#3/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52#3/r1.claim: The narrative omits an implied event: Moses cast his staff and it swallowed everything the magicians had brought, or something similar.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52#3/r1.anchor: في خلال هذه الآيات تقدير وحذف يدل عليه ظاهر القول فالمقدر من ذلك هنا فألقى موسى عصاه فالتقمت كل ما جاؤوا به

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52#3/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52#3/r2.speaker: رُوي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52#3/r2.claim: The magicians became certain of Moses’ prophethood and that the event came from God after seeing the staff unaffected by sorcery, transform, consume the props, then return to its former state.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52#3/r2.anchor: وروي أن السحرة لما رأوا العصا لا أثر فيها للسحر ثم رأت انقلابها حية وأكلها للحبال والعصي ثم رجوعها إلى حالها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52#3/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52#3/r3.claim: Hārūn precedes Mūsā to make verse endings align; Ibn Atiyya compares the delayed shattā in 20:53 for the same reason.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52#3/r3.anchor: وقدم هارون قبل موسى لتستوي رؤوس آي السور فنقل معنى السحرة وهذا كقوله عز وجل: أزواجا من نبات شتى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p302#3/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p302#3/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p302#3/r6.claim: Experienced sorcerers knew Moses's feat was neither magic nor trickery but undeniable truth, possible only for the Creator who says “Be,” and they prostrated and believed in the Lord of the worlds.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p302#3/r6.anchor: علموا علم اليقين أن هذا الذي فعله موسى ليس من قبيل السحر والحيل، وأنه حق لا مرية فيه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p302#3/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p302#3/r7.speaker: ابن عباس وعبيد بن عمير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p302#3/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas and Ubayd ibn Umayr say the sorcerers began the day as sorcerers and ended it as righteous martyrs.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p302#3/r7.anchor: ولهذا قال ابن عباس، وعبيد بن عمير:كانوا أول النهار سحرة، وفي آخر النهار شهداء بررة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p302#3/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p302#3/r8.speaker: محمد بن كعب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p302#3/r8.claim: Muhammad ibn Ka'b estimates that the sorcerers numbered eighty thousand.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p302#3/r8.anchor: قال محمد بن كعب: كانوا ثمانين ألفا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p302#3/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p302#3/r9.speaker: القاسم بن أبي بزة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p302#3/r9.claim: Al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza estimates that they numbered seventy thousand.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p302#3/r9.anchor: وقال القاسم بن أبي بزة: كانوا سبعين ألفا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p302#3/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p302#3/r10.speaker: السدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p302#3/r10.claim: Al-Suddi estimates that they numbered a little over thirty thousand.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p302#3/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p302#3/r11.speaker: الثوري عن عبد العزيز بن رفيع عن أبي ثمامة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p302#3/r11.claim: Al-Thawri, transmitting through Abd al-Aziz ibn Rafi from Abu Thumama, gives the number as nineteen thousand.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p302#3/r11.anchor: وقال الثوري: عن عبد العزيز بن رفيع، عن أبي ثمامة: كان (2) سحرة فرعون تسعة عشر ألفا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p302#3/r12.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p302#3/r12.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p302#3/r12.claim: Muhammad ibn Ishaq says they numbered fifteen thousand.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p302#3/r12.anchor: وقال محمد بن إسحاق: كانوا خمسة عشر ألفا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p302#3/r13.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p302#3/r13.speaker: كعب الأحبار
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p302#3/r13.claim: Ka'b al-Ahbar says they numbered twelve thousand.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p302#3/r13.anchor: وقال كعب الأحبار كانوا اثني عشر ألفا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p302#3/r14.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p302#3/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p302#3/r14.claim: An Ibn Abbas report transmitted by Ibn Abi Hatim says seventy men who began as sorcerers ended the day as martyrs.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p302#3/r14.anchor: عن عكرمة، عن ابن عباس قال: كانت السحرة سبعين رجلا أصبحوا سحرة وأمسوا شهداء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p303/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p303/r1.speaker: الأوزاعي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p303/r1.claim: Al-Awza'i says that when the sorcerers fell prostrate, Paradise was raised for them until they saw it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p303/r1.anchor: قال الأوزاعي: لما خر السحرة سجدا رفعت لهم الجنة حتى نظروا إليها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p303/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p303/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p303/r2.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says they saw their abodes being built for them while they prostrated.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p303/r2.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير قوله: {فألقي السحرة سجدا} قال: رأوا منازلهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p303/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p303/r3.speaker: عكرمة والقاسم بن أبي بزة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p303/r3.claim: Ikrima and al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza give the same account that the sorcerers saw their abodes being built as they prostrated.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p303/r3.anchor: وكذا قال عكرمة والقاسم بن أبي بزة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p77#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p77#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p77#2/r1.claim: The commentary marvels at the reversal: the sorcerers threw their ropes and staffs in disbelief, then soon threw themselves down in gratitude and prostration.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p77#2/r1.anchor: سبحان الله ما أعجب أمرهم . قد ألقوا حبالهم وعصيهم للكفر والجحود ثم ألقوا رؤسهم بعد ساعة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p77#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p77#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p77#2/r2.claim: One report says the converts did not raise their heads until they saw Paradise and Hell and the reward of their inhabitants.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p77#2/r2.anchor: وروي : أنهم لم يرفعوا رؤوسهم حتى رأو الجنة والنار ورأوا ثواب أهلها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p77#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p77#2/r3.speaker: عكرمة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p77#2/r3.claim: ʿIkrima says that while they prostrated God showed them the places in Paradise to which they would go.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p77#2/r3.anchor: وعن عكرمة : لما خروا سجدا أراهم الله في سجودهم منازلهم التي يصيرون إليها في الجنة

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p412#2/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p412#2/r15.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p412#2/r15.claim: The sorcerers prostrated in obedience to God and affirmation of Moses.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p412#2/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p412#2/r16.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p412#2/r16.claim: They meant the Lord whom Aaron and Moses called them to worship, who is Lord of them and all creation.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p412#2/r16.anchor: أي بالرب الذي دعا إليه هارون وموسى , لأنه رب لنا ولجميع الخلق

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p412#2/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p412#2/r17.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p412#2/r17.claim: A report says the sorcerers did not raise their heads until they saw Paradise and the reward of its people.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p412#2/r17.anchor: فقيل إنهم , ما رفعوا رؤوسهم حتى رأوا الجنة وثواب أهلها

MUQATIL:20:69-71/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:69-71/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:69-71/r5.claim: God caused the magicians to fall face down in prostration when the serpent swallowed the ropes and staffs.
MUQATIL:20:69-71/r5.anchor: فلما التقمت الحبال والعصى ألقاهم الله، عز وجل، على وجوههم سجدا

MUQATIL:20:69-71/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:69-71/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:69-71/r6.claim: There were seventy-three magicians, and their chief was named Shamʿūn.
MUQATIL:20:69-71/r6.anchor: وكانوا ثلاثة وسبعين ساحرا أكبرهم اسمه شمعون

MUQATIL:20:69-71/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:69-71/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:69-71/r7.claim: “We believe” means “we affirm”; they affirm the Lord of Aaron and Moses.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p61/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p61/r1.speaker: الأخفش
NASAFI-FULL:v3p61/r1.claim: Al-Akhfash says their quick prostration looked as though they were thrown down: they threw ropes in denial, then their heads in thankful worship.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p61/r1.anchor: قال الاخفش من سرعة ما سجدوا كانهم ألقوا فما أعجب أمرهم قد ألقوا حبالهم وعصبهم للكفر والجحود ثم ألقوا رؤسهم بعد ساعة للشكر والسجود

NASAFI-FULL:v3p61/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p61/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p61/r2.claim: A report says they saw Paradise and their homes while prostrating, then raised their heads.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p61/r2.anchor: روى أنهم رأوا الجنة ومنازلهم فيها في السجود فرفعوا رؤسهم

NASAFI-FULL:v3p61/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p61/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p61/r3.claim: Aaron precedes Moses here for rhyme; wāw does not require order, unlike the sequence in al-Shuʿarāʾ.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p61/r3.anchor: وإنما قدم هرون هنا وأخر في الشعراء محافظة للفاصلة ولأن الواو لا توجب ترتيبا

QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r21.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r21.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r21.claim: The magicians prostrated at the extraordinary power they witnessed: the staff swallowed their ropes and sticks, a load of three hundred camels, then returned to being a staff; only God knew where the objects went.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r21.anchor: فإنها ابتلعت جميع ما احتالوا به من الحبال والعصي وكانت حمل ثلاثمائة بعير ثم عادت عصا

QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r22.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r22.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r22.claim: The author points back to al-Aʿraf for this account of the staff and its swallowing the magicians' devices.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r22.anchor: وقد مضى في «الأعراف» هذا المعنى وأمر العصا مستوفى.

BURSEVI:v5p311/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p311/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p311/r1.claim: The fa is explanatory: after the staff swallowed the objects and events unfolded, the magicians were thrown down prostrate.
BURSEVI:v5p311/r1.anchor: {فألقى السحرة} الفاء فصيحة أي : فإلقاه فوقع ما وقع

BURSEVI:v5p311/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p311/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p311/r2.claim: Their falling is called being cast, as if someone hurled them, matching the earlier casting of their implements and emphasizing the force of their fall.
BURSEVI:v5p311/r2.anchor: حال كونهم {سجدا} ساجدين كأنما ألقاهم ملقي لشدة خرورهم

BURSEVI:v5p311/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p311/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p311/r3.claim: The Persian narrative says Moses' staff became a serpent and swallowed the tools; the crowd fled, Moses caught it and it reverted, and the magicians recognized a miracle rather than magic and sincerely prostrated.
BURSEVI:v5p311/r3.anchor: مردم ازترس روى بكريز آوردند وموسى اورا بكرفت همان عصا شد

BURSEVI:v5p311/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p311/r4.speaker: رئيسهم
BURSEVI:v5p311/r4.claim: The chief magician reasoned that their tools had always remained after they beat people; if Moses' feat were magic, their tools should still be there. Their disappearance showed a creator and confirmed Moses' mission, so they repented and prostrated.
BURSEVI:v5p311/r4.anchor: روي أن رئيسهم قال : كنا نغلب الناس وكانت الآلات تبقى علينا

BURSEVI:v5p311/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p311/r5.speaker: جار الله
BURSEVI:v5p311/r5.claim: Jār Allāh marvels at the contrast: they cast their ropes for disbelief, then cast down their heads in gratitude and prostration.
BURSEVI:v5p311/r5.anchor: قال جار الله : ما أعجب أمرهم القوا حبالهم للكفر والجحود

BURSEVI:v5p311/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p311/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p311/r6.claim: The verb قالوا is an explanatory resumption specifying what they said while prostrating.

BURSEVI:v5p311/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p311/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p311/r7.claim: They mention Aaron before Moses to keep the rhyme and avoid mistaking Moses for Pharaoh, who raised him, if Moses were named alone or first; Aaron is secondary in the phrasing.
BURSEVI:v5p311/r7.anchor: تأخير موسى عند حكاية كلامهم لرعاية الفواصل ولأن فرعون ربى موسى

BURSEVI:v5p311/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p311/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p311/r8.claim: Adding their Lord to the two messengers means He is the one they call to and the one who performed the extraordinary acts through them.
BURSEVI:v5p311/r8.anchor: ومعنى إضافة الرب إليهما أنه هو الذي يدعوان إليه وأجرى على يديهما

BURSEVI:v5p311/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p311/r9.speaker: بعض الكبار
BURSEVI:v5p311/r9.claim: A Sufi authority says devotion to God frees the heart from ego's claims, brings sincerity, certainty and divine lights; the magicians were drawn to God and believed by proof rather than imitation, while Pharaoh saw no proof of lordship.
BURSEVI:v5p311/r9.anchor: قال بعض الكبار : من كان له استعداد النظر إلى عالم الغيب

ALUSI-FULL:v16p287#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p287#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p287#2/r2.claim: The magicians’ prostration shows that God may grant guidance and arrival to Him very quickly; recent penitents can attain spiritual perfection, despite ignorant critics’ disbelief.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p287#2/r2.anchor: فيه إشارة إلى أن الله تعالى يمن على من يشاء

RAZI-FULL:v22p74#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p74#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p74#2/r1.claim: The magicians' prostration shows that Moses' staff became a serpent and swallowed their magic; expert magicians recognized the act as outside their craft.
RAZI-FULL:v22p74#2/r1.anchor: دلالة على أنه ألقى ما في يمينه وصار حية تلقف ما صنعوا

RAZI-FULL:v22p74#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p74#2/r2.speaker: رئيسهم
RAZI-FULL:v22p74#2/r2.claim: Their chief reportedly argued that their tools remained when they lost ordinary contests; if Moses' feat were magic, where were the objects they had cast?
RAZI-FULL:v22p74#2/r2.anchor: ويقال : قال رئيسهم كنا نغالب الناس بالسحر وكانت الآلات تبقى علينا

RAZI-FULL:v22p74#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p74#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p74#2/r3.claim: The chief's reasoning takes the objects' transformation as evidence for an all-knowing, powerful Creator and the feat on Moses' hand as proof of his true prophethood; the magicians therefore repent, believe, and prostrate in utmost submission.
RAZI-FULL:v22p74#2/r3.anchor: فاستدلوا بتغير أحوال الأجسام على الصانع العالم القادر وبظهورها على يد موسى

RAZI-FULL:v22p74#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p74#2/r4.speaker: الأخفش
RAZI-FULL:v22p74#2/r4.claim: Al-Akhfash explains أُلقيوا as a figure for speed: they prostrated so quickly that they seemed to be thrown down.
RAZI-FULL:v22p74#2/r4.anchor: التأويل فيه ما قال الأخفش وهو أنهم من سرعة ما سجدوا كأنهم ألقوا

RAZI-FULL:v22p74#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p74#2/r5.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v22p74#2/r5.claim: The Kashshaf contrasts their two acts of casting: they had just thrown ropes and staffs for disbelief, then soon threw down their heads in gratitude and prostration.
RAZI-FULL:v22p74#2/r5.anchor: وقال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : ما أعجب أمرهم قد ألقوا حبالهم وعصيهم

RAZI-FULL:v22p74#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p74#2/r6.speaker: رُوي
RAZI-FULL:v22p74#2/r6.claim: An unattributed report says they did not raise their heads until they saw Paradise, Hell, and the reward of their inhabitants.
RAZI-FULL:v22p74#2/r6.anchor: وروى أنهم لم يرفعوا رؤوسهم حتى رأوا الجنة والنار ورأوا ثواب أهلها

RAZI-FULL:v22p74#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p74#2/r7.speaker: عكرمة
RAZI-FULL:v22p74#2/r7.claim: Ikrima reports that while prostrating, God showed them the places in Paradise where they would eventually dwell.
RAZI-FULL:v22p74#2/r7.anchor: وعن عكرمة : لما خروا سجدا أراهم الله في سجودهم منازلهم

RAZI-FULL:v22p74#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p74#2/r8.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v22p74#2/r8.claim: Al-Qadi calls Ikrima's report remote: seeing Paradise directly would compel belief and undermine the voluntary faith expressed in their plea for forgiveness.
RAZI-FULL:v22p74#2/r8.anchor: قال القاضي : هذا بعيد لأنه تعالى لو أراهم عيانا لصاروا ملجئين

RAZI-FULL:v22p74#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p74#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p74#2/r9.claim: Razi replies that Abraham, despite certainty of forgiveness, still said he hoped God would forgive him; the magicians could similarly speak of hope after a vision.
RAZI-FULL:v22p74#2/r9.anchor: لما جاز لإبراهيم عليه السلام مع قطعه بكونه مغفورا له أن يقول

RAZI-FULL:v22p74#2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p74#2/r12.speaker: التعليمية
RAZI-FULL:v22p74#2/r12.claim: The Ta'limiyya infer that because the magicians say they believe in the Lord of Aaron and Moses, knowledge of God comes only through the Imam; Razi calls this weak and says their wording has other benefits.
RAZI-FULL:v22p74#2/r12.anchor: التعليمية احتجوا بهذه الآية وقالوا : إنهم آمنوا
